summary: Questions whether the promise of artistic research as a new academic paradigm matches its actual practice, examining the concept's persistent lack of shared definition and the particular tensions it raises in theatre and performance research. Menotyra 24(2), 2017; open access, English-language PDF.
relevance: A critical counter-voice from inside the field to the atlas's founding methodology texts (Frayling, Borgdorff) — it interrogates the artistic-research paradigm rather than advocating for it.

author: Hadiyan Yusuf Kuntoro
work: Glitch Art Sebagai Refleksi Memori Manusia yang Rapuh: Sebuah Penciptaan Karya Seni
summary: Documents the making of a glitch-art work through nine creative-process stages, 'data-bending' digital image data with an audio editor (Audacity) as a metaphor for fragile human memory. Gorga: Jurnal Seni Rupa 13(1), 2024 (Indonesian; open access, CC BY-SA).
relevance: A first-person practice-based account of technical error deliberately induced and turned into method — extends the atlas's coverage of artistic-research primary texts from Southeast Asia, a stated gap.

author: Arianna Gass
work: Glitch as a Trans Representational Mode in Video Games
summary: Reads three video games' use of glitch aesthetics — remediated signal noise and error — as a representational mode for transgender embodiment, dissociation and dysphoria, distinct from broader queer-games frameworks. Media-N 20(1), 2024; open access, CC BY-SA.
relevance: Treats glitch not as failure but as a generative expressive method, the same register the atlas already holds for Menkman's glitch studies, here applied to trans representation in games.

author: Giorgio Franceschelli, Mirco Musolesi
work: On the Creativity of Large Language Models
summary: Applies Boden's novelty/value/surprise framework and the classic four-P model (product, process, press, person) to large language models to ask whether they can be considered creative, separating 'easy' from 'hard' problems in machine creativity. Published in AI & Society, open access (CC-BY).
relevance: Gives the atlas a philosophically grounded account of what would have to be true for a machine to count as creative, the theoretical counterpart to the self-consuming-loop findings already anchored here.

author: Anna Jordanous, Bill Keller
work: Modelling Creativity: Identifying Key Components through a Corpus-Based Approach
summary: Uses statistical NLP on a corpus of creativity-research writing to derive fourteen components that recur across definitions of creativity, building a corpus-grounded model for evaluating computational-creativity systems. Published in PLOS ONE, open access (CC-BY).
relevance: A method for deriving creativity from evidence rather than stipulation, ballast against asserting creativity in the atelier's own works rather than measuring it.

author: Ahmad Beltagui, Andrew Bell, Marina Candi
work: A Sociomaterial Perspective on Epistemic Objects in Design Practice
summary: Field interviews across three design organizations identify four characteristics, fidelity, investment, ambiguity, history, that make an artefact function as an epistemic object holding a team's incomplete knowledge open rather than closing it. Published in Design Studies, open access (CC-BY).
relevance: Extends Rheinberger's epistemic-things line, already anchored here, from the laboratory into design practice, a direct bridge for a session that treats its own working notebook as an epistemic object.

author: Laila Rosa, Isabel Nogueira
work: O que nos move, o que nos dobra, o que nos instiga: notas sobre epistemologias feministas, processos criativos, educação e possibilidades transgressoras em música
summary: Two composer-performers examine their own songwriting through postcolonial feminist epistemologies, using their creative process to discuss gender and racial exclusion in music and academia. Portuguese-language article in Revista Vórtex, open access (CC BY 4.0), with accompanying audio files.
relevance: Fills the atlas's flagged gap in Latin American artistic-research voices and ties feminist epistemology directly to a documented creative process rather than to theory alone.

author: Craig Batty, Marsha Berry
work: Constellations and Connections: The Playful Space of the Creative Practice Research Degree
summary: Examines how doctoral candidates in creative-practice research move between conceptual thinking and material production, arguing the resulting space is productively messy rather than a failure of rigor. Published in Journal of Media Practice, open access (CC-BY) via Figshare.
relevance: A methodology text on tolerating unresolved, playful process, the institutional counterpart to the atelier's own refusal to treat an unfinished session as failure.

author: Duncan Pritchard
work: Ignorance and Inquiry
summary: Argues against standard accounts that define ignorance as mere absence of knowledge or true belief, proposing instead that ignorance is an intellectual failing of inquiry itself. Published in American Philosophical Quarterly; the journal version is paywalled, but the given repository URL hosts a free accepted-manuscript PDF.
relevance: Sharpens the atlas's not-knowing axis with a contemporary analytic account of what ignorance is, alongside Firestein's practitioner view and Cusanus's docta ignorantia.
